currentContext.expansion: Expansion in FY2025-26 was concentrated on the estate base rather than new tea capacity. The Company operates nine tea estates with their respective Tea Estate Factories in Assam over a total plantation area of about 5605.02 hectares, and in continuation of its programme of rationalisation of operations and improving profitability it disposed off the Deohall Tea Estate and Balijan (North) Tea Estate units during 2025-26. The principal new-asset project was renewable energy: Solar Power Plants were successfully commissioned in May 2025 in the remaining Tea Estates in South Bank, which the Company says will reduce dependence on captive power generation and help achieve sustainability with net zero emission in its manufacturing facilities. Alongside this, old manual stoking coal fired heaters were replaced with Thermax Hot Air Generators with Chain Grate Strokers, APFC panels were installed for power factor optimisation, electronic energy efficient gas burners were installed, all factories, hospitals, bungalows and staff quarters adopted a 100% LED lighting policy, and irrigation at Bahipookri Tea Estate was converted from diesel to electric. The main capacity-diversification project is multi crop at Duamara Tea Estate on a total area of 14.61 hectares — turmeric planted across 13 hectares and trial plots of ginger, cocoa, areca nut and Assam lemon on the balance 1.61 hectares — with production of turmeric and ginger expected during the winter season of Financial Year 2026-27. Offshore, the Company continues to run tea and macadamia operations through wholly owned subsidiaries outside India.

risks.note: The crop depends to a large extent on weather conditions and weather is of prime importance for the industry; production often fluctuates due to the vagaries of the weather, including excessive rains, drought and hail storms.

risks.risk: Fixed plantation area — yield is the only lever
risks.note: With the plantation area being constant, yield depends on irrigation facilities, better soil management techniques and weather, so growth must come from yield and quality rather than acreage.

risks.risk: Pest and disease attack on plantations
risks.note: Management must constantly ensure protection of plantations against attacks by pests, alongside adequate irrigation and soil enrichment.

risks.risk: Rising cost of production and statutory input costs
risks.note: Production cost comprises inputs statutorily required to be met, including those under the Plantation Labour Act and Minimum Wages Act, plus levies imposed by Central and State authorities; increasing cost of production is putting margins under pressure.

risks.risk: Unfair competition from the un-organised sector
risks.note: Competition from the un-organised sector is contributing to a difficult phase for the industry, which expects effective incentives from the Authorities.

risks.risk: Increased global supply and economic slowdown
risks.note: Increased supply in the global market and a slowdown of economic growth may adversely affect the Company's business prospects.

The tea industry is labour intensive and provides employment to a very large segment of the local population; as on March 31, 2026 the Company employed about 9,158 employees including workers, staff and sub-staffs, making labour cost and industrial relations structurally material.
Tea is a seasonal industry — the manufacturing process starts around mid March and continues till mid December, concentrating production and cash generation within part of the year.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company's main business is the manufacture and sale of tea, a seasonal industry in which manufacturing runs from around mid-March to mid-December and the crop depends largely on weather conditions. It operates nine tea estates with their respective Tea Estate Factories, all located in Assam, with a total plantation area of about 5605.02 hectares, and sells tea through auction centres at Kolkata and Guwahati as well as through bulk / private sales. Alongside Indian tea, the Company runs offshore operations in tea and macadamia and has taken up multi-crop cultivation (turmeric, ginger and trial plots of cocoa, areca nut and Assam lemon) at Duamara Tea Estate.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Tea:** Tea sold through auction centres at Kolkata and Guwahati, Tea sold through bulk / private sales
- **Multi-crop (Duamara Tea Estate):** Turmeric, Ginger, Cocoa (trial plot), Areca Nut (trial plot), Assam Lemon (trial plot)
- **Offshore operations:** Tea, Macadamia

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Domestic Indian tea market — tea is described as a common man's drink consumed widely throughout the country
- Auction centres at Kolkata and Guwahati
- Bulk / private sale buyers
- Offshore (outside India) operations conducted through wholly owned subsidiaries

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The outlook for the tea industry is positive due to increasing domestic demand
- Total production of tea is almost sufficient to meet domestic internal demands
- Margins are under pressure due to increasing cost of production
- Unfair competition from the un-organised sector is putting the industry through a difficult phase; the industry expects effective incentives from the Authorities
- Weather is of prime importance for the industry and production often fluctuates due to the vagaries of the weather
- With plantation area constant, yield depends on irrigation facilities, better soil management techniques and weather
- Increased supply in the global market and a slowdown of economic growth may adversely affect the Company's business prospects
- Tea is a seasonal industry — manufacturing starts around mid March and continues till mid December
- Production cost comprises inputs statutorily required to be met, including those under the Plantation Labour Act and Minimum Wages Act, plus levies imposed by Central and State authorities

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Upgrade operations at the tea estates and achieve production of quality teas to enable improved overall performance — described by the Chairman as initiatives progressing as planned
- Continue the offshore expansion programme, with efforts to increase the production capacity of Macadamia now showing results
- Improve yield and crop quality through better soil management — use of vermi compost across plantation areas, good cultivation practices and Integrated Pest and Nutrient Management on the estates
- Take up multi crop cultivation at Duamara Tea Estate (turmeric on 13 hectares plus trial plots of ginger, cocoa, areca nut and Assam lemon) to diversify beyond tea
- Continue the programme of rationalisation of operations and improving profitability, under which the Deohall and Balijan (North) Tea Estate units were disposed off during 2025-26
- Reduce energy dependence and emissions at the estates — Solar Power Plants commissioned at South Bank estates, replacement of manual stoking coal fired heaters with Thermax Hot Air Generators, APFC panels, energy efficient gas burners and a 100% LED lighting policy
- Adopt indigenously developed technologies for improvement of production in both field and factory, with continual modifications and innovations
- Solar Power Plants commissioned at the Company's South Bank tea estates to reduce dependence on captive power generation and enable sustainability in manufacturing facilities with net zero emission
- Old manual stoking coal fired heaters replaced with Thermax Hot Air Generators with Chain Grate Strokers for efficient coal burning with less carbon dioxide emission
- APFC panels installed for power factor optimisation, reducing the reactive power component and load on generators
- Electronic energy efficient gas burners installed
- 100% LED lighting policy adopted across all factories including hospitals, bungalows and staff quarters
- Conversion from diesel irrigation to electric irrigation at Bahipookri Tea Estate, reducing HSD consumption
- Use of vermi compost across plantation areas to sustain soil quality and improve yield
- Integrated Pest and Nutrient Management practices initiated on the estates
- CSR carried out through the implementing agency Dhanuka Dhunseri Foundation, with the CSR policy directed towards promoting education, healthcare, women's hostel facilities and sports (no CSR contribution was required for FY 2025-26 as the average profits of the last three financial years were negative)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion in FY2025-26 was concentrated on the estate base rather than new tea capacity. The Company operates nine tea estates with their respective Tea Estate Factories in Assam over a total plantation area of about 5605.02 hectares, and in continuation of its programme of rationalisation of operations and improving profitability it disposed off the Deohall Tea Estate and Balijan (North) Tea Estate units during 2025-26. The principal new-asset project was renewable energy: Solar Power Plants were successfully commissioned in May 2025 in the remaining Tea Estates in South Bank, which the Company says will reduce dependence on captive power generation and help achieve sustainability with net zero emission in its manufacturing facilities. Alongside this, old manual stoking coal fired heaters were replaced with Thermax Hot Air Generators with Chain Grate Strokers, APFC panels were installed for power factor optimisation, electronic energy efficient gas burners were installed, all factories, hospitals, bungalows and staff quarters adopted a 100% LED lighting policy, and irrigation at Bahipookri Tea Estate was converted from diesel to electric. The main capacity-diversification project is multi crop at Duamara Tea Estate on a total area of 14.61 hectares — turmeric planted across 13 hectares and trial plots of ginger, cocoa, areca nut and Assam lemon on the balance 1.61 hectares — with production of turmeric and ginger expected during the winter season of Financial Year 2026-27. Offshore, the Company continues to run tea and macadamia operations through wholly owned subsidiaries outside India.
